title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: The study of how chemical reactions and electricity are converted into each other.

en.text: Redox reactions transfer electrons from a reducing agent to an oxidizing agent. Electrolytic cells use electricity to drive non-spontaneous reactions, and Faraday's laws give the amounts formed. Galvanic cells use spontaneous reactions to make electricity: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode, ΔG° = −nFE°, and the Nernst equation handles non-standard concentrations. Batteries, fuel cells and corrosion are everyday electrochemistry.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Oxidation: loss of e⁻; reduction: gain of e⁻; they happen together.
Electrolytic cell: anode (+), cathode (−); electricity drives a non-spontaneous reaction.
Galvanic cell: anode (−), cathode (+); E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode > 0 for a spontaneous reaction.
Corrosion is a short-circuited galvanic cell; galvanizing and cathodic protection stop it.
